main_text.l: dissimæ[?] densissimis quasi nubibus obteguntur: aures
obsurdescunt: manus, quæ corpus custodiunt, treme-
re incipiunt: crura, quibus idem nititur, sub ponde-
re vacillant.
VIII. In ea autem quæ à fortuna manant, atque
proficiscuntur, an non vim suam atq; tyrannidem tem-
pus exercet: dum facultatibus homines exuit: dum
quos terra profert fructus conterit & corrumpit:
dum præclarorum virorum memoriam oblivione
extinguit?
IX. Iam vero rei literariæ quantam idem tem-
pus cladem intulerit, quis ignorat?
X. Quære Aristotelis plus quàm quingentos li-
bros, qui à doctis numerantur: nusquam apparebùt:
quæ rerum gestarum scriptores, quorum suis in scri-
ptis mentionem Cicero facit: non reperies.
XI. In tempore porrò corruptis depravatisq;
locis emendandis quàm viri doctissimi clarissimiq;
sunt hodie, & quàm hæc in re de literis merentur
præclarè?
XII. Ad Imperia verò & Respubl. conferre me
si vellem, Deum immortalem quàm mihi metuendū
esset, ne in orationem integram epistola excresceret.
XIII. Ubi doctæ illæ & literis literatisq; homi-
nibus affluentes Athenæ? ubi nobilis & rebus belli-
cis celeberrima Lacedæmoniorum Respublica? ubi
æmula laudis Romanæ Carthago? nonne his omni-
bus tempus solum ruinam atq; interitum attulit?

page.notes: The first word of the page, "dissimæ", is a fragment whose start is cut off at the top of the scan; the reading is doubtful. The word is printed with a long-s ligature that reads as "ß". The page number "211" is printed as "21ı" and is only partly legible. The signature at the foot reads "O 3" but the last digit is doubtful. The ampersand in "conterit & corrumpit" and "& quàm" is the printed "et" sign. The text contains no notes in the margin.
